1//! Building outlines for the navigation of the document.
2//!
3//! An outline is a tree-like structure that stores the hierarchical structure of a document.
4//! In particular, in most cases it is used to define the hierarchy of headings in the document.
5//! For example, your document might consist of two first-level headings, which in turn have
6//! more nested headings, which in turn might be nested even further, and so on. The [`Outline`]
7//! allows you to encode this behavior, and makes it easier to navigate the document in PDF
8//! viewers that support this feature.
9//!
10//! The intended usage is to create a new, empty outline in the very beginning. It represents
11//! the root of the tree. Then, you can create new outline nodes, which you can recursively
12//! nest in any way you wish while processing your document. In the end, you need to push
13//! the first layer of children to the [`Outline`] object.
14//!
15//! Finally, once you are done building your outline tree, you can use the [`Document::set_outline`]
16//! function of [`Document`] to store the outline in the document.
17//!
18//! [`Document`]: crate::third_party::krilla::Document
19//! [`Document::set_outline`]: crate::third_party::krilla::Document::set_outline
20

28/// An outline.
29///
30/// This represents the root of the outline tree.
31#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
32pub struct Outline {
33    children: Vec<OutlineNode>,
34}
35
36impl Outline {
37    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
38        self.children.is_empty()
39    }
40}
41
42impl Default for Outline {
43    fn default() -> Self {
44        Self::new()
45    }
46}
47
48trait Outlineable {
49    fn first(&mut self, item: Ref) -> &mut Self;
50    fn last(&mut self, item: Ref) -> &mut Self;
51    fn count(&mut self, count: i32) -> &mut Self;
52}
53
54impl Outlineable for pdf_writer::writers::Outline<'_> {
55    fn first(&mut self, item: Ref) -> &mut Self {
56        self.first(item)
57    }
58
59    fn last(&mut self, item: Ref) -> &mut Self {
60        self.last(item)
61    }
62
63    fn count(&mut self, count: i32) -> &mut Self {
64        self.count(count)
65    }
66}
67
68impl Outlineable for OutlineItem<'_> {
69    fn first(&mut self, item: Ref) -> &mut Self {
70        self.first(item)
71    }
72
73    fn last(&mut self, item: Ref) -> &mut Self {
74        self.last(item)
75    }
76
77    fn count(&mut self, count: i32) -> &mut Self {
78        self.count(count)
79    }
80}
81
82struct SerializedChildren {
83    first: Ref,
84    last: Ref,
85    visible_count: usize,
86}
87
88impl SerializedChildren {
89    fn write(&self, outlineable: &mut impl Outlineable, negate_count: bool) {
90        outlineable.first(self.first);
91        outlineable.last(self.last);
92
93        let mut count = i32::try_from(self.visible_count).unwrap();
94        if negate_count {
95            count = -count;
96        }
97        outlineable.count(count);
98    }
99}
100
101impl Outline {
102    /// Create a new, empty outline.
103    pub fn new() -> Self {
104        Self { children: vec![] }
105    }
106
107    /// Push a new child (which may in turn contain other children) to the outline.
108    pub fn push_child(&mut self, node: OutlineNode) {
109        self.children.push(node)
110    }
111
112    pub(crate) fn serialize(&self, sc: &mut SerializeContext, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer, root: Ref) {
113        let mut chunk = sc.new_chunk();
114        let children = serialize_children(&self.children, root, &mut chunk, sc);
115
116        let mut outline = chunk.outline(root);
117        if let Some(children) = &children {
118            children.write(&mut outline, false);
119        }
120        outline.finish();
121
122        chunk_container.non_stream.outline = Some((root, chunk));
123    }
124}

126/// An outline node.
127///
128/// This represents either an intermediate node in the outline tree, or a leaf node
129/// if it does not contain any further children itself.
130#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
131pub struct OutlineNode {
132    /// The children of the outline node.
133    children: Vec<OutlineNode>,
134    /// The text of the outline entry.
135    text: String,
136    /// The destination of the outline entry.
137    destination: XyzDestination,
138    /// Whether this node is initially open (children shown expanded).
139    open: bool,
140}
141
142impl OutlineNode {
143    /// Create a new outline node.
144    ///
145    /// `text` is the string that should be displayed in the outline tree, and
146    /// `destination` is the destination that should be jumped to when clicking on
147    /// the outline entry.
148    pub fn new(text: String, destination: XyzDestination) -> Self {
149        Self { children: vec![], text, destination, open: false }
150    }
151
152    /// Set whether this node is initially open (children shown expanded).
153    ///
154    /// If `open` is `true`, the node's children will be shown expanded when the
155    /// document is opened in a PDF viewer; if `false`, the children will be
156    /// collapsed. Leaf nodes (nodes without children) are unaffected by this flag.
157    ///
158    /// By default, this flag is set to `false`.
159    pub fn with_open(mut self, open: bool) -> Self {
160        self.open = open;
161        self
162    }
163
164    /// Add a new child to the outline node.
165    pub fn push_child(&mut self, node: OutlineNode) {
166        self.children.push(node)
167    }
168
169    pub(crate) fn serialize(
170        &self,
171        sc: &mut SerializeContext,
172        parent: Ref,
173        root: Ref,
174        next: Option<Ref>,
175        prev: Option<Ref>,
176        chunk: &mut Chunk,
177    ) -> usize {
178        let children = serialize_children(&self.children, root, chunk, sc);
179        let mut outline_entry = chunk.outline_item(root);
180        outline_entry.parent(parent);
181
182        if let Some(next) = next {
183            outline_entry.next(next);
184        }
185
186        if let Some(prev) = prev {
187            outline_entry.prev(prev);
188        }
189
190        if let Some(children) = &children {
191            children.write(&mut outline_entry, !self.open);
192        }
193
194        outline_entry.title(TextStr(&self.text));
195
196        let dest_ref = sc.register_xyz_destination(self.destination.clone());
197        outline_entry.pair(Name(b"Dest"), dest_ref);
198
199        outline_entry.finish();
200
201        // See the algorithm described in the PDF spec. When recursing down, we
202        // do not go into nodes that whose count is negative (i.e. nodes that are
203        // closed). Therefore, in case the node is closed, the visible count is
204        // just the node itself, so 1.
205
206        if self.open { 1 + children.map_or(0, |children| children.visible_count) } else { 1 }
207    }
208}
209
210fn serialize_children(children: &[OutlineNode], parent: Ref, chunk: &mut Chunk, sc: &mut SerializeContext) -> Option<SerializedChildren> {
211    let mut visible_count = 0;
212
213    if !children.is_empty() {
214        let first = sc.new_ref();
215        let mut last = first;
216
217        let mut prev = None;
218        let mut cur = Some(first);
219
220        for i in 0..children.len() {
221            let next = if i < children.len() - 1 { Some(sc.new_ref()) } else { None };
222
223            last = cur.unwrap();
224
225            let child_visible_count = children[i].serialize(sc, parent, last, next, prev, chunk);
226            visible_count += child_visible_count;
227
228            prev = cur;
229            cur = next;
230        }
231
232        Some(SerializedChildren { first, last, visible_count })
233    } else {
234        None
235    }
236}
